comment: This professor has haunted me throughout my time at Richmond. I took him my first semester freshman year, and he was very unclear with grading, belittled my writing abilities, and relied too heavily on participation. Please save yourself. I did learn a good amount, though.

Professor Miller is a very intelligent person with lots of knowledge to share. He's a bit of an acquired taste but once you get used to him he's wonderful. Bring caffeination to class because he speaks in a way that can put some to sleep. It's heavy reading but very helpful. He doesn't give you grades for essays but gives very clear feedback.

Do not take him! He assigned over 100 pages of reading a week, which is crazy for an intro level class.  He did not give us letter grades for papers, so I was unsure of my grade the whole semester.  Additionally, he is very uptight about needing to participate, and makes the whole class a discussion.  Save yourself from the stress of this class.

I think he's a good teacher. We have 3 big essays spread out, 2 in-class debates, and 2 self assessments. We have no midterm or final exam. On average we read about 100 pages a week so the class definitely can be intense at time. Overall though, I think he does his best to be fair and has been available to provide detailed feedback on assignments.

Dr. Miller was probably the worst professor to take for a first-year class. Participation is crucial but he will criticize you if you do not say what he wants. Papers are difficult and he grades harshly while also giving no clear instruction. No tests but instead you grade yourself and he changes it, if he feels he needs to (which he will).

Would not recommend for an intro class. Took intro to public policy. Rubrics for papers are unorganized and unclear with little to no direction, and debates are the same. Participation is a big part of grades, but he criticizes responses, even if they're right, and draws on background knowledge that many or most students didn't have. Hard grader.

Dr. Miller sets unrealistic goals for his students and grades based on only a few papers, which you never receive the grades of.  He also does not respond to many emails and relies heavily on class participation. I would not recommend.

Hardest class I've taken at UR, apparently easier with other profs. Nice guy but tough professor with an obscure grading system. Grades on papers are the only things in the gradebook other than 2 self-assessments. Rarely responds to emails. Always answers questions in class. Participation in class is necessary. Expects a lot for an intro course.

Professor Miller is very knowledgeable, and his lectures are packed with information. His grading system is different, he uses self assessments, and this personally pushed me to try my hardest on my papers, attendance, meeting during office hours, and in class discussion. Not many students got an A, but if you try you will. Heavy readings.
